messages:
maria: Quick heads up — new customer 'orbit' (org-orbit-prod) is aiming to kick off a pilot in ap-northeast-8 next Tue. We need GPU capacity there: asking to enable p5 (p5.24xlarge family) and g5 (g5.48xlarge family) support across accounts aws-1234 (prod) and aws-5678 (staging). Initial concurrent target: 6 p5 + 4 g5, but plan for headroom up to 12 accelerators. Also need ENI + EIP headroom for node scale. Can infra raise the service limits and seed a small capacity reservation?

jay: Which exact quotas should I put in the support case? also need account IDs, VPC/subnet info, and whether we want On-Demand or Reserved for pilot.

maria: Put both accounts (aws-1234, aws-5678). Region ap-northeast-8. Request On-Demand limits first — pilot needs predictable perf; we'll evaluate reserved/commit later. Quotas: "We need Accelerator count (p5-family) to 10, Accelerator count (g5-family) to 8, EC2 instances per region to 200, Elastic Network Interfaces to 150, Elastic IPs to 20." Include note about ENI-per-instance and EFA.

toni: FYI p5/g5 instances require ENIs and high ENI counts per node. For ap-northeast-8 make sure the subnet size can allocate 2 IPs per instance extra (EFA) and NAT throughput scaling. Also confirm SG rules and limit on NAT Gateways (we might need 2 NATs for HA).

infra-bot: quota-scan report for aws-1234 (ap-northeast-8):
```
Accelerator (p5-family) current: 0
Accelerator (g5-family) current: 0
EC2 instances (standard) current: 50
Elastic Network Interfaces (region) current: 50
Elastic IPs current: 5
```
Suggested support-case template:
```
Subject: Request quota increases for pilot (org-orbit-prod) — ap-northeast-8
Body:
Please increase the following quotas for account aws-1234 in ap-northeast-8:
- Accelerator (p5-family): 10
- Accelerator (g5-family): 8
- EC2 instances (All types): 200
- Elastic Network Interfaces (region): 150
- Elastic IPs: 20
Reason: Pilot for low-latency LLM inference requiring p5/g5 accelerators; aiming for 6 concurrent p5 + 4 g5 initially with headroom for scale testing.
Case-level notes: Please expedite for pilot starting next week; include entitlement for ENI and EFA attach if required.
```

jay: I'll file the cases for both accounts now and add Toni + Maria as CCs. Planning to request temporary On-Demand capacity and ask AWS to confirm availability across AZs. Also adding a question about accelerated networking and ENI limits per-subnet.

jay: Filed case 1234567891 for aws-1234 and 1234567892 for aws-5678 — links: https://console.aws.amazon.com/support/cases#/case/?caseId=1234567891 and https://console.aws.amazon.com/support/cases#/case/?caseId=1234567892

aws-support: Thanks, we've received case 1234567891 and will review. Typical turnaround 48-72 hours; we may reach out for architecture details.

toni: Also open a ticket with networking to enlarge subnet prefix sizes (we need spare IPs) and to pre-warm NAT Gateway throughput. If AWS suggests AZ capacity constraints, ask for cross-AZ fallback plan.

maria: Can we also get a rough cost estimate for running pilot capacity (6 p5 + 4 g5 on-demand for 7 days)? We need to include in SOW.

jay: Rough calc: p5 ~ $30/hr, g5 ~ $8/hr (example region pricing, will get precise). 6*p5 + 4*g5 = (6*30 + 4*8) = 180+32 = $212/hr => ~ $35k for 7 days (24/7). I'll follow up with precise numbers.

maria: Perfect. Assigning @jay to own the AWS cases and followups. I'll coordinate with Product for pilot acceptance criteria once quotas are confirmed.

jay: Taking ownership — will post status updates here. :thumbsup:

infra-bot: Reminder: if AWS requests architecture diagram include VPC, subnets, NAT, SG, IAM roles, and expected instance types + AMI IDs (use redwood-inference-base-ami-2026-02).

maria: Thanks team — please keep updates brief in this thread.
